texts.preamble: K.Srinivasan vs Union Of India Through on 24 January, 2019 Author: M.Nirmal Kumar Bench: M.Nirmal Kumar 1 In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated : 24.01.2019 Coram: The Honourable Mr.JUSTICE M.Nirmal Kumar Crl.O.P.No.3011 of 2011 and M.P.Nos.1&2 of 2011 [Orders Reserved on 02.11.2018] 1.K.Srinivasan 2.Kalyanasundaram ... Petitioners Vs. Union of India through Chief Health Inspector & Food Inspector, Chennai Egmore Railway Station, Southern Railway, Chennai 600 008. ... Respondent / Prayer: Petition is filed under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code, the records in S.M.M.F.No.4 of 2010, on the file of Xx Metropolitan Mag Building, Chennai 3 and quash the proceedings against the petitioners For Petitioners : Mr.S.Pugazhalthi For Respondent : Mr.P.T.Ramkumar Order
texts.facts: This Criminal Original Petition has been filed praying to quash the proceedings in http://www.judis.nic.in S.M.M.F.No.4 of 2010, on the file of XX Metropolitan Magistrate, Ripon Building, Chennai. The first petitioner / A1 is the Salesman and the 2nd petitioner / A2 is Licencee. 2. The short facts of the case are as follows:- On 20.04.2010, the respondent / complainant inspected the Soda Water Stall at Platform Nos.1 & 2 and took sample of Amutham Orange Soft Drink, following the procedures contemplated under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, (in short the said Act). One part of sealed sample packet was sent to Government Analyst, Food Analysis Laboratory, King Institute Campus, Guindy, Chennai on 21.04.2010 and Analysis was done between 06.05.2010 to 12.05.2010; public Analyst Report was made ready on 19.05.2010. In the label, date of manufacture is mentioned as 19.04.2010 and the best before 27.04.2010. Based on the Analyst's Report, adulteration complaint has been filed against the petitioners. But, in the present case, the samples were kept for nearly 20 days and thereafter, analysed, which cannot be relied upon. Therefore, the learned counsel for the petitioner prayed for quashment. One part of sealed sample packet was sent to Government Analyst, on 21.04.2010 and Analysis was done between 06.05.2010 to 12.05.2010. Based on the Analyst's Report, adulteration complaint had been filed against the petitioners. Further, in this case, the complaint had been filed on 09.08.2010 and cognizance has been taken by the Trial Court and the petitioners have to prove their case only by adducing evidence before the trial Court. Therefore, he prayed for dismissal of the petition. 6. It is found that on 20.04.2010, the respondent had gone to the petitioners shop, bought 12 packets / sachets of 'Amutham Orange Soft Drink, (Total 1500 ml. - each 150 ml) for Analysis purpose. The 12 sachets were divided into 3 equal parts of 4 sachets each and was wrapped, tied, pasted and sealed. Thus, the samples could not be said to be Harmonized Samples. The sealed sample packets were sent to Analyst on 21.04.2010. The sample was http://www.judis.nic.in analysed between 06.05.2010 to 12.05.2010 and the Analyst's Report is dated 19.05.2010. The report was handed over to the respondent on 31.05.2010. Sanction was obtained on 15.07.2010. From the Analyst's Report it is seen that date of manufacture is on 19.04.2010 and best before 27.04.2010. The Public Analyst has not mentioned as to how and what manner the sample was misbranded and there is no specific averment that the customers are mislead on account of misbranding and in the absence of any such clear averments, it cannot be said that the customers are mislead or misdirected. The samples have been analysed after the shelf-life in flagrant violation of regulation.
texts.arguments: 3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that the complainant had seized the samples on 20.04.2010, but the samples were analyzed only between 06.05.2010 and 12.05.2010 nearly after one month from the date of seizure, which is absolutely arbitrary, illegal and would vitiate the entire proceedings. The food item would become contaminated after the period of expiry. The learned counsel, in support of his contention, has relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Parakh Foods Limited Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh and Another reported in (2008 (4) SCC 584). 4. The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the respondent would submit that on http://www.judis.nic.in 20.04.2010, the respondent visited the Soda Water Stall at Platform Nos.1 & 2 and took samples of Amutham Orange Soft Drink, The contentions of the petitioners that, since analysis was not done before 27.04.2010, the shelf-life period, would have got expired and the Analysis Report, cannot be taken into account, is concerned, if such contention is to be accepted, no complaint can be filed against any individual selling adulteration product by fixing a short shelf-life period for their convenience. The shelf- life period has to be considered only for the purpose of consumption and not for doing analysis. Further, in the label, it is not declared as the product contains permitted synthetic food colour, Added flavours and it gives a false and misleading impression to the consumer about the product as it contains fruit by use of words and pictorial representation.
